neighbours.label: Reference to a famous scientific theory or thinker in history-of-science writing (Einstein's theory, Popper's Conjectures and Refutations, Hilbert, Newton's law), firing on the possessive or connective inside the reference, vs the same constructions about non-scientific people and works
fire: Eddington's 1919 eclipse expedition was designed to test Einstein's general theory of relativity.
Bohr's model of the atom was soon replaced by the quantum mechanics of Heisenberg and Schrödinger.
Thomas Kuhn's Structure of Scientific Revolutions changed how historians view progress in physics.
Maxwell's equations of electromagnetism unified electricity, magnetism and light.
The influential French mathematician Henri Poincaré anticipated parts of special relativity.
Planck's quantum hypothesis of 1900 was at first regarded as a mathematical trick.
Historians still debate how much Lorentz's transformations owed to the ether theory of his time.
Kepler's laws of planetary motion gave Newton the evidence he needed for gravitation.
quiet: Hemingway's 1952 novella was written in Cuba and won the Pulitzer Prize the next year.
Bach's cantatas were soon replaced in the church repertoire by newer works of his sons.
My uncle's collection of vintage records filled three shelves in the garage.
Picasso's paintings of the blue period show the poverty of Barcelona and Paris.
The influential French chef Paul Bocuse ran his restaurant near Lyon for decades.
Grandma's apple pie recipe of 1950 was at first written on the back of an envelope.
Fans still debate how much the band's second album owed to the punk scene of its time.
Austen's novels of country manners gave later writers a model for romantic comedy.

predictions: The possessive or connective inside a named theory or scientist reference reaches 0.25-0.75; the same possessive frames about playwrights, neighbours or coaches stay under 0.1.
